findings.message: [review/consistency] This actor-exclusion filter contradicts the stated invariant of the phase specs this feature was built against. Spec 1f61f624 (phase 3) constrains: "The notification set is a function of the STATE CHANGE, not of who performed it: exactly TWO notificationService.create calls for SUBMITTED and APPROVED cancellations, exactly ONE for DRAFT" and "Self-notification is not suppressed: when the cancelling actor is the resolved recipient, the notification is still written. The exactly-one rule holds regardless of actor identity." Spec 9244f013 (phase 6) repeats it: "no case may assert suppression on the basis of the actor being the recipient", and its success criterion #3 requires the DRAFT case to assert exactly one notification. The phase-6 spec (9244f013) constrains "Additive extension only: every pre-existing test case ... must remain byte-for-byte in intent — no case deleted, renamed, skipped, or weakened", and its success criterion #3 requires "a DRAFT cancellation still produces EXACTLY ONE notification (requester only) — the pre-existing DRAFT assertion is unchanged and no approver notification is added on that path." The pre-existing DRAFT case previously asserted `toHaveLength(1)` with `recipientId === REQUESTER_ID`; it now asserts zero, and the sibling case at line 988 was renamed from "sends exactly one cancellation notification for the original" to "notifies only the requester when the canceller IS the recorded approver". New indexes: standalone `status` (the existing `(employee_id, status)` cannot serve a status-only predicate — this is the first status-only access path in the codebase) and `approver_id` (recipient resolution for a cancelled APPROVED request). The queue query MUST also exclude `reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`: a cancelled-after-approval request is TWO rows, so without that predicate the reversal row is a spurious second queue entry. **NOT delivered as of Phase 1** — the delivered migration adds no `leave_requests` DDL at all; see *Phase 1 delivered* below.

findings.message:
[review/stale-spec] Stale notification count, same root cause as rule 9. Rule 5 states a SUBMITTED or APPROVED cancellation writes "two `Notification` rows: one to the requester (existing behaviour, unchanged) and one to the approver (new)". `docs/DECISIONS.md` → CLARIFY-006 (amended 2026-10-09) removes the cancelling actor from the recipient set, so the overwhelmingly common case — the requester cancelling their own SUBMITTED request — writes ONE row, not two. The built code and its test agree: `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts` asserts `expect(notificationService.inputs).toHaveLength(1)` for "notifies only the direct manager when the owner cancels a SUBMITTED request".
  Evidence: "5. A cancellation writes exactly one CANCEL `AuditLog` entry and, for a SUBMITTED or APPROVED cancellation, two `Notification` rows: one to the requester (existing behaviour, unchanged) and one to the approver (new). The approver notification is ADDITIONAL — it does not replace, merge with, …
findings.quoted_line: 5. A cancellation writes exactly one CANCEL `AuditLog` entry and, for a SUBMITTED or APPROVED cancellation, two `Notification` rows: one to the requester (existing behaviour, unchanged) and one to the approver (new). The approver notification is ADDITIONAL — it does not replace, merge with, or alter the requester notification, and it does not alter the audit entry (same action CANCEL, same entityType `'leave_request'`, same entityId = the ORIGINAL request id, same before/after state).
